quick.topic: Estimate the volume before you build
quick.summary: How to know whether a new feed is small or huge, with three numbers.
quick.takeaway: Rows a day, size of a row, days you keep.

parts.title: Estimate the volume before you build

beats.line: We are adding click data. My lead asked how big it gets. How do I know?
Three numbers, multiplied. First, rows per day.
Second, the size of one row.
That is ten gigabytes a day.
Third, how long you keep it. Two years makes about seven thousand gigabytes.
Rough ones are enough. You need to know small, large or huge.
About ten gigabytes a day, seven thousand over two years. That is large.
Now you can choose storage before it surprises you.

quiz.question: Which three numbers give a rough data volume estimate?
options: Rows per day, size of a row, days kept
Number of tables, columns and users
quiz.explanation: Multiplying rows per day by row size and by how long you keep data gives the storage needed.

quiz.question: A volume estimate is only useful if every input is exact.
quiz.explanation: Rough inputs are enough to tell whether the data is small, large or huge, which is what the design needs.
